questions.text: Do you keep an up-to-date inventory of the business-critical data sources, with named owners?
Do you measure and monitor data quality continuously, not just on specific projects?
Are there formal data privacy, retention and residency policies that are enforced and audited?
Is there a data catalog where a new analyst can find what they need in minutes, not weeks?
Do you have a standardized analytics and modeling platform, or does each team set up its own?
Do you have integration capabilities (APIs, events) that let you connect new services without a special project?
Do you practice MLOps or LLMOps in any production case (deployment, monitoring, retraining)?
Are current AI solutions designed so that the model or vendor can be replaced without redoing everything?
Do you have in-house data science, ML or AI engineering profiles, or do you only rely on external vendors?
Is there a formal AI training plan by role type, and is it being executed?
Do business-area leaders understand enough about AI to make informed decisions without delegating everything to IT?
Can you retain key technical talent (they do not leave within the first year for a better offer)?
Do AI initiatives go through a formal portfolio with prioritization and periodic review?
Are there documented quality gates between discovery, pilot, scaling and operation phases?
Is there an AI committee that periodically reviews the portfolio, risks and models in production?
Does every production solution have an identifiable owner, runbooks and a defined retirement plan?
Do important business decisions incorporate data as a natural input, not as an extraordinary effort?
Does the organization tolerate experiments that may fail without penalizing those responsible?
Is there institutional trust to honestly manage the conversation about AI’s impact on jobs?
Do executive leaders personally model the use of AI tools, not just preach it?
